verify_files does is_file + open/read(1MiB)/hashlib.update/close per file (long_d2.py:68-82,124-126); about 2,400 GIL-releasing calls per pass in the profile (open 371, read 585, update 310, DirEntry.stat 171, posix.stat 426, close 275, scandir 70).

Stress contender is a pure-Python loop that never blocks (stress.py:28-31); stress is a registered robustness requirement (parent-validation-plan.json stage changed-source-contention), stdlib-only, MPS not observed.
No setswitchinterval call exists in r11 sources; CPython 3.12.15.
Uncontended boundary 0.031 s wall = 0.031 s CPU; nine contended boundaries 4.280-16.135 s wall with 0.082-0.159 s thread CPU; every pass 273 files, 47,527,648 bytes.
Profile r1: 8.578 s wall, 0.0847 s CPU, max sample gap 0.2028 s; stress max sample gap 0.2633 s (limit 0.5 s).
Stress ran without cProfile and shows the same regime, so profiler overhead is not the cause.
project_members is 0.527 s cumulative of 8.578 s, so project-members dominance is unsupported.

hypotheses.H1_gil_handoff: Most source-supported. Verifier thread waits one switch interval (default 5 ms) to regain the GIL after each syscall behind a never-blocking Python thread; about 2,400 releases times 3.5-7 ms predicts 8-16 s.
hypotheses.H2_storage_latency: Weak: identical bytes read uncontended in 0.03 s. Not excluded for cold cache.
hypotheses.H3_scheduler_qos: Not excluded; GIL handoff wait is itself a timed condition-variable wait.
hypotheses.H4_second_waiter_monitor_thread: Not excluded; may explain 4.28 s versus 16.1 s variance.
